## What is happening
- **Since 6 April, 80.5% of PO lines arrived in full and on time.** The target is 96% and the figure before was 88.9%, so that's a drop of 8.4 pts.
- **The weekly scorecard fell from 93–98% in weeks 8–14 to 54% in week 18.** PO-line DIFOT recovered to 100% from week 20.
- **Short deliveries are the whole problem.** Every delivery was on time (100%). All 8 missed lines were short, and those lines were filled at 61.8%, leaving 1,149 units short.



## Whose problem it is: Baby Mart's
- **Our override inflated the orders.** Sam Patel (Demand Planning) entered overrides DOV-26-0415 to 0418 on 2 April ahead of the Kimberly-Clark TV campaign. They ramped the factor from 1.35x to 2.2x over weeks 15–18. The review was due 30 April, but they are all still **ACTIVE**.
- **Most of the shortfall sits on those orders.** 6 of the 16 override-sized lines were cut, and they hold 91.9% of the units short (1,056 of 1,149).
- **Kimberly-Clark shipped its normal quantity.** On the cut lines it delivered 99.9% of what the order would have been without the override. Only 14.6% of the cut units fell below forecast.
- **These 6 misses shouldn't count against Kimberly-Clark.** The supplier owns only 2 of the 8 missed lines.

| Rush orders | No late lines to test | Inconclusive |

**Stores still hold stock**, so no stockout recovery is needed. That reading is from 7 May store inventory, and the supply position behind it is modelled.

## What to do
1. **Demand Planning:** review and close or reset the four overrides, which are overdue for review, using actual campaign sell-through.
2. **Buying:** strip the 6 override-sized lines from Kimberly-Clark's scorecard. Agree campaign volumes with them before ordering against an uplift.
3. **Supply:** take up the 2 remaining misses with Kimberly-Clark through normal performance follow-up.
